question: Will the UK increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years before May 2026?
summary: Official signals indicate a 10-year baseline under Earned Settlement, suggesting a high near-term likelihood.
Objections correctly flag legislative approval and rollout timing risks that could delay implementation before May 2026.
Threshold analyses and consultations show plausible near-term action, but transitional rules and exemptions introduce timing uncertainty.

justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.93 to 0.83 to reflect non-negligible risk of delay and non-enactment by May 2026; maintained high confidence due to strong official signals and active consultation.

forecasts.reference-class: UK settlement policy reforms (Earned Settlement) proposing a 10-year baseline for settlement (ILR) with potential implementation in 2026 after consultation; applies to migrants arriving from 2021 onward, with possible reductions for high contribution.

sources.claim: The government announced that the permanent settlement qualifying period would be doubled to 10 years, applying to migrants who arrived in 2021 onwards, subject to consultation.
The Earned Settlement consultation outlines increasing the baseline qualifying period to ten years and an open consultation process (Nov 2025).
The Earned Settlement consultation page confirms the consultation and details about the plan to reform settlement rules, with a closing date for responses.

The default qualifying period for settlement will be increased to 10 years under the earned settlement model, with potential reductions based on four core pillars (character, integration, contribution, residence).
The government’s 2025 proposals would set a baseline 10-year qualifying period for many migrants, with exceptions and a time-adjustment framework depending on individual circumstances.
Migration Observatory explains the proposed 10-year wait as the baseline, with some groups facing shorter or longer periods depending on category and contributions.
Guidance states a 10-year continuous qualifying period and lists routes that count toward it (e.g., family routes, private life, long residence).
The Long Residence route requires 10 years continuous lawful presence, with time spent on various routes counting toward the 10-year qualifying period.
Guardian reports the government proposed extending the baseline wait for settlement to 10 years, potentially affecting 1.5 million migrants.
The default qualifying period for settlement would be increased from five to ten years as the baseline, with a consultation on further adjustments.
House of Commons Library notes that the government announced in Nov 2025 that the baseline qualifying period would be ten years, with exceptions.
May 2025 Guardian article states the government is proposing to extend the waiting period for permanent settlement from five to ten years for migrants.
Bevan Brittan notes the 2025 settlement reform consultation opened, outlining a ten-year baseline and earned settlement structure.
Specialist firm notes the consultation closes Feb 12, 2026 and changes could take effect as early as April 2026.
IPPR estimates that hundreds of thousands of children could face a 10-year wait under the proposed settlement timelines.
